chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl narrated from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddaq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who is fasting and has intercourse with his wife. He said: He performs ghusl, and nothing is due upon him.

So this report admits of two possibilities: one of them is that he did that absentmindedly or forgetfully, for then nothing is binding upon him and his fast has been completed. We have already clarified that in our larger book. The second is that he did that while not knowing that it is not permissible to do it in the state of fasting, and that which indicates this is:

key_terms.صَائِمٌ: a person in the state of fasting

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a fasting person has intercourse forgetfully or without knowing the ruling?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling on intercourse during fasting and presents a narration stating that ghusl is required and nothing further is due. The accompanying discussion explains that this is understood in cases of forgetfulness or ignorance of the ruling, showing a juristic reconciliation of the hadith within fasting law.
